messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT detected: capacity-tier routing anomaly for tenant 'acme-marketing'. Traffic intended for Hosted pool spilling into Dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-us-west-2) and triggering quota exhaustion. Automatic fallback loops observed between region us-west-2 <-> us-east-1. Paging oncall.
oncall-mike: Acked. I'm oncall. Looking at routing logs now. Can someone add recent ACL or routing policy changes?
kevin: I saw a recent route-policy merge 10m ago from PR #4221 that touched `prefer_dedicated_when_full` rules. Pinging @sarah who reviewed.
sarah: Yep I reviewed that PR but it was supposed to only change threshold logic. I didn't expect a tenant tag mismatch. Investigating.
carla: Symptoms: increased p95 latency for dedicated customers, elevated token cost and a few 503s for some Hosted customers who got routed to dedicated and hit tenant isolation checks.
ops-jen: Confirmed: dedicated-pool-us-west-2 logs show many requests with header `X-Redwood-Tier: hosted` — tenant tag not honored. Also seeing continuous routing decisions flipping: route -> fallback -> route -> fallback (looping), causing extra load.
oncall-mike: Immediate mitigation options: 1) pause the new route-policy, 2) quarantine affected tenant on the routing layer, 3) scale up dedicated pool temporarily. I'll do #1 and #2 now. Doing `rdrctl routing policy disable prefer_dedicated_when_full --env=prod`
kevin: :eyes: I'm running a dry-run to confirm. Also check if the policy engine cached an old model variant mapping — wrong model variant mapping could cause model mismatch too.
sarah: I see the problem. The PR changed the matching precedence so `tenant.isolation=false` got evaluated after the capacity check. That allowed Hosted requests to be eligible for dedicated fallback. Will open a rollback of precedence change.
oncall-mike: Done: policy disabled. Pushing a temporary rule to force-hosted: `rdrctl routing override add --tenant acme-marketing --force-tier=hosted --ttl=600`
ops-jen: Override applied. Monitoring metrics — traffic to dedicated pool from acme-marketing dropped by ~95% in last 30s. Dedicated CPU utilization dropping.
carla: Still seeing some 503 spikes from users whose requests were in-flight during the switch. Working with edge to return graceful fallback to hosted models where possible.
cust-success-liz: Heads-up - a few enterprise customers reported degraded response time around 16:04 UTC. I'm drafting a notification. Any ETA for full mitigation?
oncall-mike: ETA ~5-10m for stabilization. We will keep dedicated spillover blocked and then run non-destructive checks before re-enabling policy.
kevin: Root cause hypothesis: policy precedence regression + an unexpected tenant tag removal in the request proxy for some clients (proxy v2.7.1). Need to check last deploys.
sarah: Confirmed proxy v2.7.1 rolled out 15m ago to us-west-2 and included a header normalization change. That combined with precedence change caused the misroute. I'll revert precedence change and open a runtime patch to skip normalization for `X-Redwood-Tier` header.
oncall-mike: Rolling back precedence now: `git revert -m 1 5f8a3b2` -> deploying route-policy v1.14.1-rollback. Starting canary.
ops-jen: Canary succeeded on 2 nodes. Metrics look good. No loop spikes. Will continue to monitor for 10m.
carla: Forensic note: the loop was amplifying because fallback to us-east-1 then capacity checks there found slightly different available capacity and sent it back. The policy lacked stable tie-break. Add a tie-break based on tenant-id hashed region to avoid oscillation.
kevin: Logged follow-ups: rollback PR, proxy header normalization revert, add unit tests for precedence and tie-breaks, e2e that simulates partial capacity mismatches. I'll assign tickets.
cust-success-liz: I'll send a brief incident advisory to affected customers: include timeline, customer impact (latency spikes, occasional 503s for hosted requests), and immediate mitigation steps (policy disabled). ETA 20m.
oncall-mike: Post-incident: we should blacklist the tenant from dedicated fallback for 24h to let caches clear and avoid thrash. Setting `rdrctl tenant set-attr acme-marketing no_dedicated_fallback=true --ttl=86400`
ops-jen: Blacklist set. Also taking a snapshot of routing logs for the SRE postmortem: `rdrlogs query "tenant:acme-marketing AND (route:dedicated OR fallback:true)" --from=1759876400 --to=1759877400 > /tmp/acme-routing-snapshot.log`
carla: Customer impact assessment: about 27 requests failed with 503s linked to wrong-tenancy checks; estimated affected sessions ~120 in 15min window. No data exposure. Cost impact: extra dedicated token usage ~0.2% of daily spend, but tenant isolation breach is priority.
kevin: Who made the precedence change? PR author is @maria (config team). Maria - can you sync up on the follow-ups?
sarah: Adding follow-ups in triage board. We'll require owners from config, proxy, and routing to sign off before re-enabling policy.
maria (not in thread): (joining) I see the PR, sorry — my bad on missing the precedence edge-case. I'll pair with kevin to add tests and help with revert.
oncall-mike: Good. Next steps summary: 1) Allow rollback to stabilize (in progress), 2) keep tenant blacklisted for 24h, 3) customer advisory (liz), 4) postmortem and remediation tickets (kevin & sarah), 5) test coverage and deploy safer policy with tie-break logic (maria). Anyone object?
cust-success-liz: No objections. I'll include a note that Dedicated customers saw latency increases but were functionally separate — Hosted customers shouldn't have to be hit but some in-flight requests did.
ops-jen: Monitoring: all good now. Dedicated pool CPU falling to baseline, no new oscillations for 7m. Marking incident as mitigated but not resolved.
oncall-mike: I'll handoff to next oncall at 1759876740. Final note: open an incident channel with postmortem template and assign P1->P2 once we have root cause confirmed. :white_check_mark:
